title: The Unexpected Letters
premise: August Eriksen, a wedding planner who orchestrates other people's happily-ever-afters while refusing her own, is drafted by her mentor into a city pen-pal program meant to pair strangers — but a clerical error pairs her with Jonah Vale, the rival planner who nearly ruined her career and whom she blames for her brother's death. Their anonymous letters, written without knowing each other's identity, slowly strip away the armor both have built around the truth of that night. When August discovers who her correspondent is, she must decide whether loyalty to her dead brother's version of events matters more than the truth Jonah finally confesses — and whether the career she clawed her way into can survive a scandal that would expose them both. In the end, she chooses truth over the lie that saved her, testifies against her own mentor, and meets Jonah not at an altar but at a courthouse steps, where they begin something honest instead of perfect.
about_author: Bram Kavanagh is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent a decade inside other people's weddings before writing about the people who plan them. He lives in a coastal city he refuses to name, where he still answers letters the slow way, by hand.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: August's POV. She runs a flawless wedding while privately cataloguing every way love fails, reciting her belief that the heart is trainable, containable. A toast from the bride's grandmother about letters she kept for sixty years unsettles her. Emotional beat: competence as armor, and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: Assigned Correspondents
chapters.summary: August's POV. Her mentor, Delia Marsh, ropes her into the Harborline Pen-Pal Project as PR for the firm. The pairing software glitches — or is nudged — and August receives a first letter that is barbed, brilliant, and strangely familiar in its contempt for weddings. Beat: curiosity disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: The Enemy's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah Vale, drowning in debt and disgrace after the Meridian Hotel disaster, writes his assigned stranger with bitter honesty he'd never speak aloud. He almost recognizes something in the letter he receives but talks himself out of it. Beat: two people circling a fire they can't name.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: August's POV. She and Jonah clash at an industry gala, trading scalpel compliments in person while, hours later, their anonymous letters grow warmer. August notices the coincidence and dismisses it. Beat: dramatic irony tightening — the reader sees what she refuses to.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knew
chapters.summary: August's POV, with a flashback. We learn her brother Marcus died at the Meridian collapse — the gala Jonah's firm planned — and that August's testimony about Delia's safety shortcuts saved her own career and buried Jonah's. Beat: guilt she has repackaged as grief.

chapters.title: The Letter That Forgives
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah's anonymous pen pal writes something that sounds, uncannily, like absolution for a sin he never committed. He starts investigating the pen-pal program's pairing logs. Beat: hope arriving through a side door, and suspicion waking beside it.

chapters.title: Shared Air
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. August and Jonah are forced to co-plan the Whitmore-Sable wedding — the biggest contract of the year — and their professional sparring turns electric. A rainstorm traps them in a venue after hours. Beat: proximity as accelerant.

chapters.title: Containment Failing
chapters.summary: August's POV. She writes her pen pal about the co-planner she can't stop thinking about, not realizing she's describing him to him. Jonah reads it and finally suspects the truth. Beat: the dramatic irony peaks and begins to break.

chapters.title: The Pairing Logs
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah bribes a volunteer coordinator and confirms the impossible: his pen pal is August Eriksen, the woman whose testimony destroyed him — and who, he now realizes, may have lied to save Delia. Beat: betrayal and tenderness colliding in one envelope.

chapters.title: Confession in Draft
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He writes a letter confessing everything he knows about the Meridian shortcuts, including evidence that Delia ordered them, and hesitates over the signature line. Beat: the pen hovering — loyalty to the truth versus the safety of silence.

chapters.title: Delia's Favor
chapters.summary: August's POV. Delia, sensing the Whitmore contract slipping, asks August to dig up dirt on Jonah. August discovers Delia has been falsifying the pen-pal pairings all along — engineering enemies on purpose, as a private experiment in cruelty. Beat: the mentor's mask slips.

chapters.title: The Unsent Stack
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. August finds Jonah's unsent confession in a shared venue office and reads her own name in his handwriting. She flees without confronting him, carrying the letter like contraband. Beat: heartbreak and revelation in a single silent scene.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: August's POV. She weighs Marcus's memory, her testimony, her career, and Jonah. Delia pressures her to sign an affidavit recanting nothing and blaming Jonah fully. August almost signs. Beat: the price of survival made literal, in ink.

chapters.title: The Whitmore Wedding Eve
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. On the eve of the biggest wedding of their careers, Jonah learns Delia plans to pin the Meridian evidence on him permanently. He decides to go public — even if it costs August everything too. Beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Guests, One Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mid-ceremony, Delia's sabotage threatens to collapse the event — and with it both their reputations. August and Jonah work in wordless tandem to save the wedding, and in the quiet after, she returns his confession and admits she read it. Beat: the truth spoken at last, in a room full of flowers.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: August's POV. Delia offers August the firm, the name, everything — if she stays silent. August asks what Marcus would have wanted and finally hears the answer: not her survival at any cost. Beat: the theme crystallizes — loyalty to the dead cannot mean loyalty to lies.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: August's POV. She recants her old testimony before the licensing board, naming Delia and herself. The career that saved everything begins to burn down around her. Beat: climax — the cost paid in full, and strangely, relief.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Ash
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The verdict lands; Delia is barred, August is untouchable in the industry, and Jonah's name is cleared but his firm is gone. He writes one last letter to his pen pal and doesn't send it. Beat: grief with clean edges, and an open door.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: August's POV. She finds the unsent letter, reads it, and writes back — by hand, signed, no program, no alias. Beat: the romance's true confession, in ink instead of speech.

chapters.title: Courthouse Steps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Weeks later, on the steps where the board announced its ruling, they meet without a contract between them. No wedding, no client, no deadline — just two people who chose truth. Beat: quiet resolution, earned not given.

chapters.title: What the Heart Is For
chapters.summary: August's POV. August rebuilds — a tiny practice, only couples she believes in. She keeps her brother's letters and adds her own to the box. Beat: identity remade; the muscle theory revised.

chapters.title: The Unexpected Letters
chapters.summary: Epistolary coda, both POVs. A year of their real letters, unedited, ending with one that simply says: come home. The final image is a mailbox on a coastal street, and two names on one return address. Beat: the title fulfilled — love as correspondence, ongoing.
